title: Adjacent-Domain Disclosure from Public Occupancy in GBFPlus
contribution_type: protocol-specific confidentiality counterexample; archival preprint with reproducible evidence
claim: For an honest GBFPlus snapshot with one successful insertion, publicly distinguishable occupancy selects the complete share set. XORing its occupied words reveals the unmasked adjacent-domain suffix exactly. For c successful insertions, occupied count w=c*kappa certifies disjoint supports and the same scan reveals the aggregate identifier XOR.
assumptions: Honest construction starting empty; occupied words never overwritten; failed insertions do not mutate the snapshot.
Authentic successful-insertion count; genuine occupancy including occupied zero words and public word widths/share count.
Observer has permissioned-ledger read access; no regulator secret or query token.
The pinned specification permits timeout publication without a positive minimum batch count.
Repeated reads observe a frozen array; written identities hold for every admissible share realization.

The aggregate can be uninformative when all admissible histories have the same XOR.
